newsitem.title: UK: DALGETY CLIMBS ON BREAK-UP TALK IN PRESS.
newsitem.headline: DALGETY CLIMBS ON BREAK-UP TALK IN PRESS.

text.p: Shares in British petfoods and agricultural feeds firm Dalgety Plc were indicated sharply higher on Monday after weekend press speculation of a possible break-up bid for the beleagured group.
The shares were indicated 13p higher at 263-1/2p by 0720 GMT.
The Sunday Telegraph newspaper said investment bank ING Barings had been working on plans for a 900 million stg break-up bid since the company issued a profits-warning in July.

The report said among those likely to be interested in bidding for all or parts of the business were Swiss group Nestle, Ralston Purina of the U.S. and Britain's cash rich food group Associated British Foods.
Shares in AB Foods closed at 548-1/2p on Friday.
Dalgety was said to have indicated that it was not interested in any deal until the group completed its strategic review next month.

"You can come up with some quite juicy values for the group based on the potential profitability of the pet food business and the synergies with an acquirer," said David Lang, analyst at Henderson Crosthwaite, adding that 300p a share did not seem unreasonable.

"The companies mentioned would certainly be very interested in owning parts of the operation," Lang said. "The biggest and most attractive chunk would be petfoods but a number of businesses would fit very nicely with ABF."
Analysts said there was a lot of latent value within the group, but Dalgety could choose to unlock this through internal restructuring rather than a break-up.
